A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support reliable comparison; v4 also includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V3 reports original analyses of eight LLM judges across 11 rating tasks, plus synthetic experiments on selection effects, annotation budgets, and rater error.

after.justification: V4 reports original analyses with nine LLM judges across the retained 11 tasks and retains the synthetic experimental results.

M1.justification: Response-set elicitation, rating reconstruction, aggregation, and multi-label MSE evaluation remain unchanged. New Appendix G.1 explains procedures already described in Section 3.4 and Appendix D rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 tasks across Civil Comments, SNLI, MNLI, AlphaNLI, SummEval, QAGS, and TopicalChat, using content filtering and prevalence estimation. The introductory examples do not add evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The reported judge-system comparisons expand from eight models to nine through the addition of GPT o3-Mini, visible in Section 4.1 and Appendix D's ranking plots. The existing agreement-metric comparison families are retained.

E3.justification: The real-data sensitivity sweep extends from betaH = 0–0.6 to 0–0.7 (v3 Figure 4; v4 Figure 5). V4 specifies a 1024-token reasoning budget and separate rating extraction for the added o3-Mini model. Retained prompts, temperature, and ten samples per item are unchanged; the five-token output limit is newly disclosed.

E4.justification: Analyses of how indeterminacy affects selection regret extend the sensitivity range and include o3-Mini in model-specific sensitivity and rank-inversion analyses. Appendix E's annotation-budget, asymmetric-selection, and rater-error robustness experiments are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V4's checklist item 7 newly identifies the uncertainty reporting as SEM obtained through bootstrap sampling. V3 already displays error bars but does not explain their estimation method. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Real-data plots contain revised results and new o3-Mini entries. The headline toxicity example changes from Mistral Small, ranked seventh under forced choice with a reported 30% gap, to o3-Mini, ranked fourth with a 31% gap, under the expanded candidate pool. Finding 4 now reports MSE as comparable to KL-D(h,j) at zero human indeterminacy, replacing the earlier all-settings superiority statement.

T1.justification: The identifiability theorem, Appendix C's assumptions, decomposition and rank-consistency results, their proofs, and Appendix F's counterexamples are retained. Added reconstruction instructions restate existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The framework contribution, forced-choice bias claim, and four practical recommendations remain. The abstract updates the empirical headline from eight judges and 30% to nine judges and 31%, and the introduction adds public code/data release to the contribution statement.

C2.justification: New Appendix G.2 discusses threshold selection as a policy choice, precision versus false-negative tradeoffs, and misleading agreement near extreme thresholds. The conclusion newly connects retained rater-error findings to reduced deliberation requirements. One new G.2 sentence incorrectly reverses which class predominates at low versus high thresholds.

D1.justification: V3 points to supplementary code and main.ipynb; v4 documents a public code/data location and quickstart tutorial. V4 also adds token limits, reasoning-output handling, inference cost and timing, and stepwise reconstruction guidance. These mostly expand documentation rather than establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 refines the comparison with Elangovan et al. by explicitly distinguishing inter-rater disagreement captured by soft labels from intra-rater indeterminacy captured by response sets. The cited-work inventory and extended literature coverage remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and part of Related Work are rewritten to explain intra-rater indeterminacy more explicitly. V4 regularizes terminology, adds Appendices G.1–G.2 and a conference checklist, and updates the conference header, while preserving the overall scientific organization.

P2.justification: V4 adds an introductory illustration adapted from existing appendix examples, redraws the toxicity and framework diagrams, and expands plot legends and axes. It separates the extended-results and sensitivity plots, corrects SummEval labels, and removes v3's compact aggregation table while retaining its definitions elsewhere.

improvement.justification: V4 improves reproducibility through fuller inference details, public code/data instructions, and explicit bootstrap-SEM reporting. It also corrects the main SummEval example to Relevance and more carefully qualifies MSE's advantage at zero indeterminacy. These limited gains outweigh the localized new threshold-direction error in Appendix G.2; the underlying framework and experimental coverage remain stable.
